4. Defendant Nos.1 to 7 and the defendant Nos.10 to 15 contested the suit by filing 2 sets of separate written statements denying the averments made in the plaint contending inter alia that their common case were that the suit land belonged to Shochidananda Sarkar and he left the then East Pakistan for India and did not exchange his lands in Bangladesh i.e. the suit lands, with the plaintiffs or anyone else. The plaintiffs in order to grab the suit lands created a forged and fictitious deed of exchange and an irrevocable power of attorney and managed to get the Genuineness ' Certificate issued by the defendant No.1 for the so-called exchange deed. The local people having come to know about of the said forged and fictitious deed of exchange and the power of attorney made complaint to the concerned authority. Upon which the then Revenue Deputy Collector, Panchagarh causing physical enquiry submitted his report finding that the deed of exchange and the power of attorney was forged and fictitious and the said deed was comprised of khash land of the Government. Their further case was that as the said Shocidananda Sarkar left for India leaving his properties uncared for, the Government declaring the suit land abandoned settled to some lands therein to Gent Barmanand others, the bargadars of Shocidananda Sarkar in various Settlement Cases who had been possessing the suit lands on payment of rents. In the suit lands there were Government Food Godown, Sub-Registrar Office, residence of Government Medical Officer and Thana Health Inspector. As the plaintiffs were engaged in grabbing the Government properties, notice was served upon the plaintiffs asking them to show cause as to why the Genuineness Certificate issued on 29-4-1989 and the registered deed No.4398 dated 20-5-1989 regularizing the exchange deed in their favour would not be cancelled. The plaintiffs having received the notice appeared and prayed for time to show cause and time was granted but they did not show any cause. Consequently, the defendant No.1 passed the impugned order dated 26-7-1993 for cancellation of the Genuineness Certificate issued earlier and the registered deed rightly and properly. The defendant Nos.10 to 15 purchased some lands out of the suit lands from the Geru Bartman and others and their successors by Kabalas and had been possessing the same erecting dwelling house thereon. Plaintiffs had no right, title, interest and possession over the suit lands and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 22. As the suit lands are not included in the list of Enemy. Properties, at present Vested Pioperties, under section 9(1) or as per the sub-section 6 of the section 9 of Arpito Sampatti Pratyarpan Ain (Act No.23 of 2011), the same are not vested properties. Government is estopped by law from claiming it to be vested property. And the private party-respondents no. 10-15 who are claiming through Government as lessees not at the strength of vested property. It is to be noted further that the Government followed the procedure laid down in section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 to treat and take over the property earlier vide Miscellaneous Case No.354/8/60-61 and another Miscellaneous Case No.770/8/60-61 thereby followed the procedure to take over the property and leased out the same as khas land. So, the first ground does not come to play, rather, this ground is nugatory. 

 24. The argument advanced by the learned Senior Counsel for the appellant regarding transposition of the Government from the respondent to petitioner seems to us that not the correct exposition of law. It is true at the  instance of the Government, there is no civil revision, however, it would not be out of juncture to reflect here, the real stream of conscienceless of the Government machineries because the Government has to act through its machinery which is not so active as like as private litigant, who can move promptly, freely, and fairly, rather, it is most difficult and cumbersome to activate the executive machineries and authorities to seek redress against the private litigant, the instant case is not exception to that characteristic, seeing such unusual behavioral act of the local administration only to secure the ends of justice and resolve the real controversy of the case, the learned Judge of the High Court Division applied the theory of due process to render the justice. Therefore, it cannot be said in activating of theory of due process, the High Court Division committed any legal infirmity. There is no such law that when any of the litigating party challenged the same judgment wherein the Government was made opposite party as the Government is the necessary party, not only that the Government contested the suit by filing written statement and on appeal, decree actually was passed against the Government when the Government machinery is reluctant to act in accordance with law, the Court not do incoherence in securing the justice, in other words, when due to incoherence of the Court justice not only defeat, rather, act of fraud would be legalized using the process of the Court. The Government, therefore, can be transposed as the petitioner from the opposite party to secure the justice. 

 27. Now, in the present case, the factssheet and scenario just opposite to the earlier facts sheet of the case because after an enquiry by the Deputy Commissioner, Panchagarh, it was unveiled that the deed of exchange being Deed No.3260 of 1960 on what basis the present Deed No.4398 dated 30-7-1979 was made and obtained by the predecessors of the plaintiffs-appellants that was forged and no land was exchanged by that deed between the above parties. Thus, it was obligatory to the Deputy Commissioner, Panchagarh to pass an appropriate order regarding that deed. Accordingly, the Deputy Commissioner passed the order and cancelled the deed in view of the prevailing condition given in the deed itself empowering the Deputy Commissioner to determine the deed if it is found that any fraud practice has been occurred in obtaining the deed from the Government. Now, the question is whether the order of cancelling the deed is genuine or not, if it was found that cancellation is not genuine on the basis of enquiry in that score, it can say that the executive acted illegally defying the earlier judgment and order of the Court of law but if it is established that earlier events the predecessors of the appellants had practiced fraud in obtaining the deed in question that unveiled after proper enquiry, in our view that it is not review of the earlier judicial discussion and decision, rather, passed the order in view of new cause of action which within the dominion of the executive. Had it been discovered in the earlier occasion that fraud practice was committed in obtaining the deed in question? Can the predecessors of the appellants can get the decree in their favour under the judicial review, the answer is obviously no. In this regard this Division's view is that the legislature, executive and judiciary have to function with their own spheres demarcated under the Constitution. No organ can usurp the functions assigned to another. Function of democracy depends upon the strength of independency of State organs. Legislature and executive have the powers maintenance, distribution and control of finance of the State. Judiciary has the power to examine and to ensure that aforesaid two organs of the State functionaries have been working within their constitutional limits and in accordance with law. The Constitution does not permit the Court to direct or advice the executive in the matter of policy or to sermonize qua any matter which under the Constitution lies within the sphere of legislature or executive, provided these authorities do not transgress their constitutional limits or statutory powers. Judiciary also must guard against encroaching the limitations. The scope of Judicial enquiry is confined to the question whether the decision taken by the Government is against any statutory provisions or is violative of the fundamental rights of the citizens or is opposed to the provisions of the Constitution. It is the executive and legislature who are entitled to frame policies and take such administrative decision as they think necessary in the public interest. The Court should not ordinarily interfere with policy decisions, unless clearly illegal or unconstitutional. 

 44. It reveals from the factsheet of the present case that it is undeniable admission from all the parties that Shachida Nanada Sarkar was the original owner of the suit property who left the erstwhile East Pakistan in the year 1960 migrating India who never came back from India to the then East Pakistan or Bangladesh. The property in question was taken over by the then administration on behalf of the State. Thereafter, some property was leased out to some persons. After that the whole property was transferred to the predecessors of the appellants. Before that, few official buildings were constructed over some portions of the property and those offices till now running by the Government official. In the meantime, the earlier lessees of the Government also claiming their possession over the suit property. The facts also revealed that the predecessors of the present appellants also claiming that they are in possession of the suit property but not in accordance with law.
